newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to implement telecom deregulation plan.
newsitem.headline: Israel to implement telecom deregulation plan.

text.p: The Israeli government will set up a committee shortly to implement plans to deregulate the last remaining monopoly segments of the telecommunications industry, a Communications Ministry spokesowman said on Sunday.

The go-ahead to form the committee came after Friday's cabinet meeting, at which ministers unanimously approved the recommendations of an inter-ministerial committee to open up basic and inter-urban telephone service and telecommunications infrastructure to competition.
"The government decision on Friday opens the way to full-scale competition in line with the committee's recommendations," the spokeswoman said.

She said the government also agreed to hold talks on the plan with unions representing Bezeq Israel Telecom workers. The unions are opposed to further liberalisation and joined last week's general strike to protest it.
State-owned Bezeq now has a monopoly on the sectors due to be opened to competition.
The committee will have until the end of this year to produce a plan for implementing liberalisation. The government's goal is to open the segments to competiton by the end of 1998.
